name: MAUSAM (मौसम)
line: India's real seasons as four numbered issues a year, each with one house crew, three named colours and one cover on every Westside surface.
role: The spine of the year. Each issue sets the palette, cast and cover for its season. Garmi and Baarish are standalone shoots. Tyohaar is Dehleez Edition 01 and Shaadi is Five Functions Edition 02, so the frame needs no second production.
format: Each issue ships 12 to 16 portrait stills.
Six-second 9:16 loops come from the same shoot.
The issue page in the app and on westside.com shows each look in stock at the member's home store.
The cover becomes the WestStyleClub WhatsApp header.
A printed issue card sits at every cash desk.
Garmi is stills and loops only.
Two issues are built around film: Baarish has one film, and Shaadi has the five Five Functions Edition 02 episodes.
The Baarish film is silent, 45 to 60 seconds long, shot in one Mumbai stairwell.
Tyohaar's 60-second Dehleez film is cut from the threshold portrait sessions.
cadence: Four issues a year (Garmi, Baarish, Tyohaar, Shaadi), numbered from Mausam No. 01.
No. 01 Garmi, 'Linen Hours': April to May 2027, on the first Friday after the Pilot 01 go/no-go, in the pilot city cluster only.
No. 02 Baarish, 'Slate, Moss, Wet Sand': first week of July 2027, as The Window goes national.
No. 03 Tyohaar: Dehleez Edition 01, Navratri to Bhai Dooj 2027. One Indian artist designs every Westside threshold (311 today) as a toran and side panels.
No. 04 Shaadi: Five Functions Edition 02, mid-November 2027.
Garmi and Baarish covers go up in two waves, a week apart.
Each issue posts on a Thursday, and its cover opens in the Window bays the next day.
channels: @seenatwestside: the Thursday season slot. Issue day posts a run of 6 to 9 frames with little or no caption, and the members' preview of the new Window follows at 9 PM. The loops and remaining stills fill the following Thursdays of the season. For Tyohaar and Shaadi the slot runs as Dehleez and Five Functions. @westsidestores shares the cover to Stories and as a Collab post, and keeps offers, launches and store news. Also: the app and westside.com home and issue page, the WestStyleClub WhatsApp header, The Window bay in issue week (wave A, then wave B), the cash-desk card, and OOH only around that season's store openings.
cast: 8 to 10 faces per issue, drawn from FRONT ROW's 30 New Faces, Seen In discoveries and two Westside store stylists. Every issue includes at least one sitter over 50 and spans regions and sizes. We propose Westside's chief creative (Umashan Naidoo) as house creative director, with one external photographer, stylist and art director held for at least four issues. Beauty by Studiowest, credited.
store_hook: In issue week the cover is that week's Window: in the pilot city cluster for Garmi, and in every store's Window bay from Baarish. Wave A stores get it first and wave B stores a week later. Members preview it on @seenatwestside at 9 PM on Thursday, and it opens on Friday. The app's issue page shows each look in stock at the member's home store. The code on the cash-desk card books a 30-minute Mausam fitting (BOOK) or holds a size (HOLD) at that store. For Tyohaar the bay carries the Dehleez capsule look, and Window numbering continues.
kpi: Footfall per store (entries) in issue week. For Garmi and Baarish, wave A stores against wave B stores that do not yet have the cover. For every issue, like-for-like against the same weeks last year, not the previous four weeks, because the season itself moves demand. Store actions: Mausam fittings booked and attended, and sizes held and collected, per store. Also 14-day sell-through of the cover looks per store. Tyohaar and Shaadi are also read as Dehleez and Five Functions.
art_direction: Shoot one real Indian location per issue as architecture, with no added props. Garmi: a brutalist corridor in Chandigarh at noon. Baarish: a Mumbai stairwell in real rain.
Use daylight from one direction and keep the shadows. Shoot Baarish only in real overcast weather, never in a studio.
Put one figure in each frame, full-length or three-quarter, at 3:4 and 9:16, with headroom. Never cut at the hem, and never put product grids on the cover.

Name three colours on the cover (Garmi: bone, khaki, indigo. Baarish: slate, moss, wet sand. Tyohaar: marigold, kohl, ivory. Shaadi: mehendi green, sangeet midnight, reception ivory). Reuse them on window planes, the trial-room wall, signage, the WhatsApp header and the film grade.

Put Westside's own wordmark top left, with 'MAUSAM No. 02 / BAARISH' beneath it in small uppercase sans and the numeral in the serif. A hairline Devanagari मौसम is the second mark. City cuts carry the city's script.
Put no price, offer or call to action on any image, and give every post full magazine credits.
precedent: Zara Studio launched as a premium capsule in fall 2016. From SS22 to SS26 a stable core crew has made it: Steven Meisel, Baron & Baron under Fabien Baron, Karl Templer, Pat McGrath and Guido Palau. The film genre changes each season and the palette is named (SS26, March 2026: powder blue, sage, blush), and Zara's windows team describes renewing the windows with each campaign. Target relaunched @TargetStyle at New York Fashion Week on 13 September 2025 around one named fall campaign, 'Forever Fall'. Mausam keeps the fixed crew, the named palette and the named season, and gives them India's four seasons, which a two-season SS/FW calendar does not cover.

name: THE WINDOW
line: Every Friday one numbered look goes into one window bay and onto @seenatwestside, and the full look waits on a rail just inside the door.
role: The weekly cover and newness signal, on the glass every passer-by sees. It is built to lift footfall across Westside's existing stores, not only at openings, and every install doubles as a store test.
format: Each store gives one window bay to one look family on one to three mannequins.
The look comes from one own label a week, in rotation: E.T.A., Utsa, Vark, Wardrobe, Nuon and Bombay Paisley.
The look is built and photographed in one reference store.
It ships on Tuesday as a VM kit sized for small mall bays, and stores install it on Thursday night.
The full look, in all sizes, waits on a Window rail just inside the door for seven days.
Assets: one 3:4 still, a 6-second 9:16 loop, a WhatsApp header crop and the Google Business Profile photo.
An A5 rail card carries the number, the label and a QR code to HOLD.
cadence: Weekly, at store opening every Friday.
Members see it first in the Thursday preview at 9 PM.
Numbered continuously from Window No. 001, one a week.
Every nine Windows make one nine-frame grid.
Pilot 01 (January to March 2027): the launch store only. The First Look maker's object holds its bay for weeks 1 to 4, and Window No. 001 opens in week 5.
Every later opening follows the same rule: the maker's object holds the bay for the first four weeks.
After the go/no-go with Trent, the Mausam No. 01 Garmi cover (April to May 2027) is the Window in the pilot city cluster, in two waves a week apart.
National from July 2027, with Mausam No. 02 Baarish.
The national install runs in two waves: wave A stores on Friday, wave B stores the following Friday.
In a Mausam launch week, the Window is the issue cover.
From Navratri to Bhai Dooj 2027 (Dehleez Edition 01), the bay carries the Dehleez capsule look and the numbering continues.
channels: @seenatwestside: the Friday series. One grid frame of the reference window goes up at store opening and ends in HOLD, with Stories of local versions from stores in different cities. The members' preview runs in the Thursday 9 PM slot. @westsidestores shares each Window to Stories with a link to the style handle, and brand moments run as Collab posts; offers stay on @westsidestores and never appear in the bay. In store: one window bay in every Westside (311 stores at 30 September 2026) and the Window rail just inside the door. Also: the Thursday-night preview to WestStyleClub members on each store's WhatsApp, an app home tile, each store's Google Business Profile photo, updated the same morning, and window screens in flagships looping the 6-second film.
cast: Mannequins only, no models. We propose Westside's chief creative (Umashan Naidoo) as house creative director, credited on every Window. One house photographer shoots the reference window each week. Each store's VM lead is credited 'Dressed by' on the local version.
store_hook: The full look, in all sizes, waits on the Window rail just inside the door for seven days. Members see it on Thursday at 9 PM. Reply HOLD 047 to your own store's WhatsApp, or scan the rail card, and your size is held until Sunday close.
kpi: Footfall per store (entries), Friday to Sunday: wave A stores against wave B stores, which install the same Window a week later. In Pilot 01, the launch store against its matched control stores. Store action: HOLDs per store per week, and the share collected by Sunday close. Also: seven-day Window-rail sell-through against the rest of the floor.
art_direction: One look from one label, on at most three mannequins. Every form is fully dressed: drape, bag, footwear and jewellery.
The backdrop is the current Mausam colours as flat plaster or paper planes, and nothing else.
No SALE vinyl, festoons or props ever touch the bay.
The number is the only graphic on the glass: 'No. 047' in the house serif, about 30 cm high, bottom left.
Shoot straight on at mannequin eye height at 7 AM, before the mall opens, at 3:4.
Use the same angle in the same reference store every week, so the archive reads as one grid.
Light with warm 3000K top light and one side wash. Reflections in the glass are allowed; gels and LED chasers are not.
precedent: The numbering borrows from Zara SRPLS: numbered collections from CLLCTN 02 (Spring 2019) to CLLCTN 16 (April 2026), under one credited creative director, Karl Templer, with Craig McDean shooting it repeatedly since 2019. SRPLS releases twice a year. The weekly beat is Westside's own: in July 2026 Bloomberg reported that an AI design suite lets Westside's in-house designers produce 400 to 500 designs a week, up from about 50. The store showcase borrows from Target, whose redesigned SoHo store opened its first phase on 9 December 2025 with The Drop, a rotating showcase for monthly style collections. The reference-store method borrows from Zara's full-scale pilot stores at headquarters, where a full-time team mocks up stores and windows (Business Insider, 2018).

name: THE TRIAL ROOM
line: A Westside store stylist, a real member and one brief, filmed through the curtain of a named store's trial room, ending in BOOK.
role: The conversion series on @seenatwestside. A weekly episode and fortnightly bylined columns turn watching into a booked trial room at a named store. In Pilot 01 it is the only property in the three cluster stores, so it gives the like-for-like read.
format: Each weekly episode is a 45 to 60 second vertical film plus a five-frame carousel.
A member arrives with a brief, the stylist passes three looks through the curtain, and the member chooses at the mirror.
Titles use the member's own words, as in No. 012, 'My brother's sangeet, and no lehenga'.
Each stylist writes a bylined column every fortnight: 250 to 300 words and six to eight phone portraits shot to house rules.
Column headlines name the store and city, as in Column No. 007, Bandra, Mumbai: 'One raincoat, five monsoon commutes'.
Live stock at that store sits under every column image.
Every episode and column ends on 'Book <stylist> at <store>'.
BOOK holds a trial room for 30 minutes with the looks pulled in your size.
Style Call is the optional first step: a 15-minute WhatsApp video call that converts to a booked room.
cadence: Episodes post every Wednesday on @seenatwestside, numbered in seasons of 12 from Trial Room No. 001.
Columns run fortnightly from each bylined stylist, and each quarter's columns are collected as one Trial Room volume.
Briefs rotate monthly: office, monsoon, college, festive and wedding guest.
Pilot 01 runs for eight weeks at the first Q4 FY27 opening (January to March 2027), with 4 Westside store stylists, one in each pilot store.

The launch store runs every property in the pilot: First Look, The Window, The Trial Room, Seen In and The Regulars. The three cluster stores run The Trial Room only. Each store is read against matched control stores.
@seenatwestside premieres on preview night, the evening before the launch store opens, and @westsidestores announces it the day before.
The readout comes at opening plus 10 weeks, followed by a go/no-go with Trent.
After a go, year one grows to 30 to 50 stylists, one per new-format store, and no further until quality holds.
channels: @seenatwestside, Wednesday slot: the episode as a Reel with its carousel, ending in BOOK. In column weeks the column follows as a carousel in the same slot. @westsidestores keeps offers, launches and store news, and shares each episode to Stories or as a Collab post. Other surfaces: a named Trial Room section in the Westside app and on westside.com, where each column sits with that store's live stock; the WestStyleClub WhatsApp list, where each episode arrives with a BOOK button; Collab posts with the stylist's own handle; Shorts on Westside's YouTube channel; and screens beside the trial rooms in Trial Room stores.
cast: Westside store stylists, bylined with their home store. Pilot 01 has 4, one per pilot store. Real WestStyleClub members of any age and size, cast through a WhatsApp casting call, paid, with signed releases and guardian consent for anyone under 18. Store staff appear as themselves. Members of YNG, a 4,000-member community, as reported in Trent's Q4 FY26 investor presentation, host the college season and write one guest column per Mausam issue.
store_hook: Message 'BOOK 012' to that store's WhatsApp. The stylist pulls the episode's three looks in your size and holds the trial room for 30 minutes on a day you choose. Bring a friend. Not sure yet? Ask for a 15-minute Style Call on video first. Each store publishes its open slots every week and replies within an agreed time. The counter captures your WestStyleClub ID with the code.
kpi: Footfall per store (entries) in Trial Room stores against matched control stores. In Pilot 01 the three cluster stores are the like-for-like read. Then, per store and stylist: BOOK count from episodes, columns and Style Calls; show-up rate; share of booked visits that end in a bill, matched by WestStyleClub ID; average bill of booked visits against walk-ins at the same store; and repeat bookings within 90 days.
art_direction: The curtain is the frame. Shoot from outside the room with the curtain half drawn: a sliver of mirror, a hand passing a hanger. Show full length only on the reveal.

Pilot and new-format stores share one house room spec: one hook, one stool, a full-length mirror, a wall in the season's colour, and a warm 3000 to 3200K panel in place of the tube light. The room number is stencilled on the door.
Shoot on a fixed phone rig at chest height, never a handheld selfie. The stylist directs and the rig shoots.
Cast real members of any age and size, never models. Studiowest make-up stays natural, with no beauty filters. Faces may be cropped for privacy.

Column bylines read 'THE TRIAL ROOM, COLUMN No. 007 / BY <NAME>, WESTSIDE <STORE>, <CITY>'. The essay is in sentence case and label names are in small capitals. Prices appear only in the shop edit, never on a portrait or in the film.
Sound is room tone and the curtain rail. The season's track plays only on the reveal.

Hero image: a half-drawn ivory curtain and a hand passing a Utsa kurta through the gap. In the sliver of mirror, a woman in her forties is laughing. The door reads 'TRIAL ROOM 4 · WESTSIDE <STORE>', with a small byline in the corner.
precedent: In June 2026 Zara launched The Fold-er, four bylined columns inside zara.com and its app, each illustrated with the author's own photos and a shop link under every image. Zara's Nanjing flagship opened on 21 March 2025 with a 'fit check' studio, fitted with multiple cameras and lighting settings and booked through WeChat, where shoppers film their own looks. Zara's AI Try-On, launched in December 2025, passed 7 million sessions by Inditex's FY2025 results on 11 March 2026, which shows how strongly 'will it suit me' drives use. Westside answers the same question with a person in a named store, and ends in a booked trial room.

name: SEEN IN
line: Every Saturday, in a different priority city each week, a white seamless goes up on the pavement outside one Westside, the neighbourhood is photographed in its own clothes, and the prints hang in that store a week later for the subjects to collect.
role: Always on, a city a week, and the Monday series on @seenatwestside. It is the cheapest beautiful property in the set and a footfall lever for mature stores. It is also the casting engine for Mausam, First Look and The Regulars. It starts in Pilot 01 at the launch store.
format: 12 to 20 full-length portraits on a 2.4 m white seamless outside one Westside.
One 30-second voice clip: 'what are you wearing and why'.
A carousel and a Reel, posted on Monday and ending in RSVP SEEN.
The following week, a printed portrait wall goes up at the host store's entrance.
Each subject collects a framed print of their portrait at the billing counter.
cadence: Weekly slot: Monday on @seenatwestside. At full scale each Monday is a different city, so each of the six priority cities comes round about every six weeks.
Shot on a Saturday afternoon and posted on the Monday. The wall goes up in the host store the following week.
Pilot 01 (Jan to Mar 2027): it shoots at the launch store on the opening Saturday and again in week 5. The Mondays in between carry the wall going up and the subjects collecting their prints.
After the go/no-go with Trent, it adds cities until each Monday is a different one.
Festival specials: Durga Puja in Kolkata, and Ganesh Chaturthi in Pune and Mumbai.
It also runs on the opening Saturday at every full-tier First Look.
channels: Lives on @seenatwestside in the Monday slot: the carousel and Reel, ending in RSVP SEEN to the host store's WhatsApp to see the wall. The Saturday shoot appears in that day's in-store Stories. @westsidestores shares each episode to its Stories or as a Collab post, and keeps its own grid for offers, launches and store news. Also carried on the Westside app, on city-segmented WestStyleClub WhatsApp, and on the host store's entrance wall.
cast: Passers-by and shoppers in their own clothes, across generations. Local Regulars act as street-casting scouts. Westside's house photographer shoots it, or a trained YNG member working to the same spec. (YNG is a 4,000-member community, as reported in Trent's Q4 FY26 investor presentation.) Everyone signs a release, and minors need guardian consent.
store_hook: The prints go up in the host store a week later, under a dated title ('SEEN IN SALT LAKE, 17 OCT'). Neighbours RSVP SEEN to see the wall. Each subject collects a framed print at the billing counter with an RSVP code, gets a WestStyleClub invite, and is invited to bring the family.
kpi: Footfall per store (entries) at the host store in wall week, against matched control stores in the same city. Store actions: RSVP SEEN replies and framed prints collected at the billing counter. Also tracked: new WestStyleClub sign-ups at collection and family group size on collection visits.
art_direction: Put a 2.4 m chalk-white seamless on the pavement in open shade and use daylight only. Keep the street and the Westside fascia visible at the edges, so the address is in every frame.
Shoot full length and centred, with the same focal length and camera height every month in every city, so the archive reads as one.
The cover frame is black and white. The carousel is in colour.
Caption formula: first name, age, neighbourhood and one quote, with honest credits for everything worn, including non-Westside pieces ('Saree from my nani, jacket from Westside').
Every set includes at least one person over 55 and one teen or child, because Westside is a family store.
The wall title follows one formula: SEEN IN, the neighbourhood, the date.
precedent: Seen In is Westside's own format: the neighbourhood, cast on its own pavement. The look borrows from Zara Studio's Spring/Summer 2025 campaign, 'On the Road' (March 2025): rough black-and-white studio portraits that reference Richard Avedon's In the American West. Zara cast that campaign with models. Seen In keeps the discipline of the frame and casts the people who shop at the store behind it.

name: FIRST LOOK
line: Every new Westside opens as a numbered premiere, with a preview night for its pin codes, one local maker's object alone in the window and the store team as its masthead.
role: Rolling, at every new Westside, in two tiers: the full programme for new cities, flagships and new formats, and a kit for infill stores. It is the vehicle for Pilot 01. Openings are where Westside is growing: Trent guided to about 50 new Westside stores a year at its June 2026 AGM.
format: The full tier is for new cities, flagships and new formats.
Preview night is the evening before opening, for 250 to 400 members who RSVP by pin code on WhatsApp.
A FRONT ROW culture-shaper from the city hosts, and city press attend.
A commissioned object by a local maker stands alone in the window bay for weeks 1 to 4.
The store team is photographed as the store's masthead.
The first 30 customers on opening day are photographed at the entrance.
On the opening Saturday, a Wesness run finishes at the store where the city has a chapter.
That afternoon, Seen In shoots at the door and posts on Monday.
The 72-hour Burst runs within 5 to 8 km of the store.
From week 5 the window bay passes to The Window.
The kit tier, for infill stores, keeps preview night, the window object, the entrance portraits and the 72-hour Burst.
cadence: Every opening from Pilot 01 onwards. Each edition carries the store's place in Westside's count, in three digits, as in First Look No. 330 (Westside had 311 stores on 30 September 2026, so the first Q4 FY27 opening is likely to be about No. 330).
Openings arrive in clusters. Westside opened 23 stores in Q4 FY26, added 1 net in Q1 FY27 and 10 net in Q2 FY27, so crews are planned for 20 or more openings a quarter.
Pilot 01 is the first Q4 FY27 opening (January to March 2027) and runs for eight weeks.

The launch store runs every property in the pilot: First Look, The Window, The Trial Room, Seen In and The Regulars. Three cluster stores run The Trial Room only and give the like-for-like read. Each is measured against matched control stores.
Pilot 01 uses 4 Westside store stylists and about 15 to 30 catchment Regulars. It reads out at opening plus 10 weeks and ends in a go/no-go with Trent.
In every opening store the maker's object holds the window bay for weeks 1 to 4, and The Window takes the bay from week 5. In the Pilot 01 store, Window No. 001 opens in week 5.
channels: @seenatwestside: the opening series. It sits outside the weekday slots and premieres on preview night, the evening before each store opens. In Pilot 01, @seenatwestside itself premieres that night. Through the opening month the new store leads Saturday's in-store Stories (RSVP), and its opening-Saturday Seen In posts in the Monday slot, ending in RSVP SEEN to see the wall. @westsidestores announces each preview night the day before, carries the opening as store news, and shares the premiere to Stories or as a Collab post. Elsewhere: a countdown on the hoarding; WestStyleClub WhatsApp to members in the catchment, by pin code; the 72-hour Burst of geo-paid Instagram and YouTube within 5 to 8 km, with local Regulars and city pages; city press; and the new store's Google Business Profile.
cast: The new store's team, introduced by name, including its Westside store stylists; WestStyleClub members in the catchment, invited by pin code; a cohort of catchment Regulars (about 15 to 30 in Pilot 01); one FRONT ROW culture-shaper from the city as host; one local maker or craft cluster; and the city's Wesness chapter, where one exists.
store_hook: Members reply 'RSVP 330' to the new store's WhatsApp to join preview night, by pin code. They can also BOOK a first-hour trial room before the doors open on opening day. The first 30 customers are photographed at the entrance, and their prints are handed over when they come back a week later. Every guest leaves with a numbered card for a first Style Call within 30 days: a 15-minute WhatsApp video call that converts to a booked trial room.
kpi: Footfall per store (entries): weeks 1 to 8 entries per sq ft at the new store, against the opening curves of comparable recent openings in the same city tier, drawn from waves such as Q4 FY26. Store actions: RSVPs per store, the share who attend preview night, and first-hour BOOKs. Then: new WestStyleClub members in the catchment; the 30-day return rate (portrait collections and Style Call card redemptions); and first-month sales against plan. Pilot 01 reads out at opening plus 10 weeks.
art_direction: The store number is the logo of the opening week: 'No. 330' in the house serif on the hoarding, invitation, bag sticker and first post, with the city name in its own script beneath.
The hoarding is the teaser: plain uppercase lines only, such as 'No. 330. OPENS FRIDAY.' over the neighbourhood's name, with no renders and no faces.

Shoot the store empty and fully lit the night before, as one dead-symmetrical frame from the entrance, with the team lined up between the rails as the cast photograph. This is the premiere frame on @seenatwestside.

One local maker's object stands alone in the window bay for weeks 1 to 4, with no product beside it: bidri in Hyderabad, kantha in Kolkata, cane and bamboo in the north-east. No balloon arches, ribbon or 'Grand Opening'.

Photograph the first 30 customers at the entrance on a coloured seamless (from Mausam No. 01, a colour of the current issue), with the same lens, height and distance at every opening, so the openings build one archive.
The invitation is a letterpress card with the store number and address, mirrored exactly in the WhatsApp invite.
precedent: Zara premieres its big collections in one time-boxed room; First Look borrows the room and gives it to a new store. Re{form} Zara by John Galliano, Vol. 1 was shown by appointment, booked through zara.com, in a hôtel particulier at 70 rue des Archives in the Marais (1 to 6 October 2026). Bad Bunny's Zara collection was previewed at a pop-up in Plaza Las Américas, Puerto Rico, on 16 May 2026, five days before its global launch. The 50 Creators pop-up at 40 avenue George V, Paris (2 to 5 October 2025) added talks and a café before the collection went on sale on 6 October 2025. Numbering by store count follows Trent's own practice of announcing stores by number, as in its press release for the 243rd Westside store, in Jaipur (early 2025).

name: DEHLEEZ (दहलीज़)
line: Every Diwali one named Indian artist designs the threshold of every Westside store (311 today) as a toran and side panels, and in 50 stores families book a free portrait at it in their festive best.
role: Westside's annual festive tentpole, running from Navratri to Bhai Dooj. It is also Mausam's October issue, No. 03 Tyohaar, one of Mausam's four issues a year. It spreads the festive moment across every door instead of concentrating it in one flagship.
format: A numbered annual edition, starting with Dehleez Edition 01 at Diwali 2027.
One Indian artist designs every Westside threshold (311 today) as a toran and side panels.
Any floor print is a border only, never a motif to stand on.
The artist co-designs a small capsule across Utsa, Vark, Bombay Paisley and Studiowest.
The Window bay carries the Dehleez capsule look, and Window numbering continues.
In 50 portrait stores, trained store teams run a portrait studio at the threshold in off-peak hours.
A 60-second film is cut from the sessions: 30 families at 30 thresholds, with regional-language cuts.
The artwork, music and film pass a cultural review before release.
cadence: Annual, from Navratri to Bhai Dooj.
Edition 01 runs at Diwali 2027 as Mausam No. 03 Tyohaar, after the Pilot 01 go/no-go with Trent.
August 2027: the artist is announced.
Thresholds install in two waves, wave A then wave B.
Portrait slots open three weeks before Diwali.
Every Thursday of the run, Dehleez takes the season slot on @seenatwestside.
From mid-November 2027 the slot passes to Mausam No. 04 Shaadi, which is Five Functions Edition 02.
Diwali 2026 (8 November) sets the baseline: Westside records festive footfall per store.
channels: @seenatwestside: the Thursday season slot for the whole run, from the artist's door to the family portraits and the film. The members' Window preview at 9 PM on Thursday shows the Dehleez capsule look in the bay. @westsidestores: the capsule launch and the list of portrait stores as store news, with each Dehleez post shared to Stories or as a Collab post; the August 2027 artist announcement runs as a Collab post on both handles. Elsewhere: the 311 thresholds and Window bays; WestStyleClub WhatsApp for portrait booking and delivery; Hindi, Marathi, Telugu, Kannada, Bengali and Assamese cuts; art and design press as well as fashion press; OOH near flagships.
cast: One artist a year, drawn from FRONT ROW or a living craft tradition, and named as large as Westside. WestStyleClub families across generations and regions. Westside store stylists help families style themselves from the capsule. Store teams work as the portrait crew, trained by the house photographer. YNG members who are photographers join the crew in the portrait stores (YNG is a 4,000-member community, as reported in Trent's Q4 FY26 investor presentation).
store_hook: BOOK a free 10-minute family portrait on WhatsApp at a Dehleez portrait store near you, with a Studiowest touch-up first. Families arrive dressed, or Westside store stylists style them in store from the capsule. They leave with a printed portrait, and the file arrives on WhatsApp within 24 hours.
kpi: Footfall per store (entries) from Navratri to Bhai Dooj, like-for-like against the Diwali 2026 baseline, read wave A against wave B across the two install waves. Portrait BOOKs per store: slots booked and slots attended. Also per store: average family group size; bills from portrait families on the day; Dehleez capsule sell-through; posts geotagged to the store.
art_direction: The threshold is the only decoration: a toran and side panels in three colours the artist chooses, never the default festive red and gold. No fairy-light clutter, marigold strings or 'Diwali Sale' near any hero image.
Keep the floor plain. Any floor print is a border only, and no motif or religious symbol sits underfoot.
Use real light: one soft 2700K key and no fill flash. Each family holds one diya: LED, or a real flame only with the mall fire officer's sign-off.
Shoot formal, frontal portraits at eye level, with the toran and side panels framing the family, like an old studio photograph.
Cast grandparents to babies, from every region and of every build. Families style themselves from the capsule with Westside store stylists.
Set 'DEHLEEZ EDITION 01' with दहलीज़ at equal size, the artist's name as large as Westside's, and the store dateline in uppercase sans. Each print carries only the family name and the store.
Commission one track, a reworked aarti or folk melody, for the film, the stores and every Reel. It goes through the cultural review with the artwork and the regional cuts.
precedent: On 15 October 2024 Zara launched 'Reverie' with the artist Jayesh Sachdev, its first collaboration in India: a Diwali capsule of tees, sweatshirts, totes and patchouli candles built around a colourful tiger motif. It was anchored by one 10-foot tiger sculpture at Phoenix Palladium, Mumbai, with display corners in New Delhi, Bengaluru, Pune and Gurugram. In September 2026 Target built its national 'Inside Out' campaign, which runs to 31 October 2026, around one owned object, the red bag. Reverie anchored the festive moment in one mall; Dehleez puts it at every Westside door, every year, and makes the threshold Westside's own object.

name: FIVE FUNCTIONS
line: Five short films in the language of the Indian wedding video, and one promise in store: show your wedding invitation and a Westside store stylist plans every function on your card in one session.
role: Westside's wedding-season property, run without a discount. From November 2027 it is Mausam No. 04 Shaadi, the November issue, and it runs to February. It turns the invitation in every Indian home into a reason to visit a store. Booked alterations build in a second visit.
format: Five films of 3 to 4 minutes each, shot in the language of the Indian wedding video.
In Edition 01 the five functions are the film structure: haldi, mehendi, sangeet, wedding and reception.
Each episode follows one real guest through one function, styled in a named Westside store.
Casting is regional, so each guest brings their own community's version of the function.
Titles read like a guest list: 'Episode 01 · Haldi · The cousin who flew in from Dubai'.
One episode premieres each Thursday at 8 PM, on @seenatwestside and in the Westside app.
Each episode is cut for Reels and YouTube Shorts, and there is no long cut.
In store, 45-minute Bring the Card sessions are booked on WhatsApp or taken as walk-ins.
The stylist plans a look for every function on the card.
Looks are held in a trial room, and alterations are booked with a collection date.
cadence: One numbered edition a year: Edition 01, then Edition 02.
In season, one episode every Thursday for five weeks, in the @seenatwestside season slot.
Edition 01 is the festive-drop alternative: one existing store, on the Jan to Feb 2027 wedding dates, against matched control stores.
The edition store's alteration capacity is confirmed before Edition 01 launches.
@seenatwestside premieres with Edition 01, Episode 01, announced on @westsidestores the day before.
Edition 02 is Mausam No. 04 Shaadi, nationwide from mid-November 2027, after the go/no-go with Trent.
Edition 02's Episode 01 lands the week before the first peak wedding dates.
Bring the Card sessions run on the Jan to Feb 2027 wedding dates in Edition 01, then from November to February each year.
channels: @seenatwestside: the Thursday season slot, one episode a week at 8 PM, an hour before the members' Window preview at 9 PM. The same evening the episode goes up in the Westside app, and its link goes to WestStyleClub members on WhatsApp, built to be forwarded to family WhatsApp groups. @westsidestores announces each edition the day before and shares each episode to Stories or as a Collab post; offers and launches stay on @westsidestores. Other surfaces: Reels and YouTube Shorts cuts, full episodes on Westside's YouTube channel, regional-language cuts, each store's WhatsApp number for BOOK, and wedding planners and venues in the edition city.
cast: Real wedding guests who are WestStyleClub members: the cousin flying in, the groom's college friend, the mausi. Every guest is paid and has given consent, and casting is regional. FRONT ROW New Faces play supporting roles. Westside store stylists and the store's alterations tailor appear as themselves.
store_hook: Show your wedding invitation at the store, printed or on WhatsApp, or BOOK ahead on the store's WhatsApp with the code CARD. A Westside store stylist plans a look for every function on your card in one 45-minute session. The looks wait in a trial room, and alterations are booked with a collection date that brings you back. Guests still out of town can start with a 15-minute WhatsApp video call that converts to a booked room. In Edition 01 this runs in the edition store; from Edition 02, at any Westside.
kpi: Footfall per store (entries) in the wedding weeks, like-for-like against last season and against matched control stores, with the January end-of-season sale matched in the controls. Store actions per store: Bring the Card sessions, booked and walk-in. Also per store: multi-function baskets (items per bill, and the share of bills above a set value), return visits to collect alterations, and episode completion.
art_direction: Play the genre straight. Each episode uses one wedding-video device, such as the slow-motion entrance, the family line-up or the varmala lift, shot with cinema restraint. No drones, lens flares or filters, and nothing that mocks the family.
Lock one colour to each function: haldi yellow, mehendi green, sangeet midnight, wedding red, reception ivory. Costume, set and title cards follow it.
Shoot at real venues at the real hour of the function, lit by the venue's own tungsten and string lights.
The trial room is the recurring set. Every episode opens on hands opening a real card, then cuts to the same Westside trial room.
Cast across communities and budgets: a Marwari sangeet, a Telugu haldi, a Bengali reception. Menswear (E.T.A. and KALA by E.T.A.) gets equal screen time.
No price, logo bug or call to action inside the film. Title cards read 'EPISODE 03 · SANGEET' with a Devanagari subtitle. Each episode closes on the store's name and city, then full credits.

Hero image: a young man in an ivory bandhgala holds a red-and-gold wedding card up to a Westside trial-room mirror, with venue string lights reflected behind him. 'FIVE FUNCTIONS · EPISODE 05 · RECEPTION' is set small along the bottom.
precedent: Zara premieres genre films on its own surfaces: 'Le Dîner' (11 Dec 2025), a roughly 15-minute Christmas film, premiered at 20:00 in the Zara app and online. Willy Chavarria's telenovela-style film 'Vatisimo' followed on 26 Mar 2026. Kate Moss's two Zara editions were each set by a real occasion: party season (30 Nov 2024), then festival season (9 Jun 2025). In India, Tanishq's Rivaah Bridal Insider (June 2025) gave each wedding function its own episode, for jewellery. Five Functions does the same for clothes, and ends in a fitting.

name: THE REGULARS
line: Westside's creator ladder on WestStyleClub: your member ID is your creator ID, your home store is your stage, and you move up on store bills and visits, not clicks.
role: The volume and community engine of @seenatwestside. It puts WestStyleClub members, YNG members, Wesness runners, FRONT ROW culture-shapers and Westside store stylists on one ladder, with one ID and one monthly brief. It carries the system's humour (The Bench) and the Westside run. At every opening, the new store's Regulars supply the local posts for the 72-hour Burst.
format: Four tiers are named after the store: FLOOR, RAIL, WINDOW and FRONT ROW.
Four tracks run across them: Stylist, Creator, Runner and Culture.
Regulars move up a tier on store bills and visits, reviewed every quarter.
Each month brings one central brief, with templates and three shot grammars: mirror, pavement and trial room.
Every post ends on a fixed 1.5-second end card: 'Seen at Westside, <store>, <city>'.
Every Tuesday, @seenatwestside features one Regular who tagged their home store.
The Bench is a monthly 'bas dekh rahe hain' brief, plus a real bench outside the trial rooms.
The Runner track is a monthly Wesness run that starts or finishes at a Westside store, in 2 to 5 km women's formats, on a numbered route card.
Each full-tier First Look adds a Wesness run that ends at the new store on its first Saturday.
Briefs and runs are numbered in three digits, for example Westside Run No. 004.
cadence: Always on: every Tuesday on @seenatwestside, ending in RSVP to Regulars Night.
One central brief a month, numbered from Regulars Brief No. 001.
One Regulars Night a month in each Regulars store, on the Thursday night the Window is installed.
Tiers are reviewed every quarter.
Pilot 01 (Jan to Mar 2027, eight weeks) runs The Regulars in the launch store only, with about 15 to 30 Regulars from its catchment.
The cohort is recruited before preview night, when @seenatwestside premieres.
The first Regulars Night is the Thursday that Window No. 001 is installed, ready to open in week 5.
After the go/no-go with Trent, each store that joins recruits three to five Regulars, and every new opening recruits a new cohort.
The July 2027 brief, 'The Window goes monsoon', marks The Window going national with Mausam No. 02 Baarish.
channels: @seenatwestside, every Tuesday: one Regular who tagged their home store, ending in RSVP to Regulars Night. Regulars also post on their own Instagram and YouTube, tagged to a named store (never just 'Westside'), and the strongest run as Collab posts with @seenatwestside. @westsidestores keeps offers, launches and store news, and shares the Tuesday post to Stories or as a Collab post. WestStyleClub WhatsApp carries the monthly brief, home-store codes and Regulars Night RSVPs. Bylined Regulars pieces sit in the app's Trial Room section. Wesness WhatsApp communities carry the run calls. Regulars Night goes to Stories afterwards and is never streamed live.
cast: WestStyleClub members. YNG members: YNG is a 4,000-member community, as reported in Trent's Q4 FY26 investor presentation. Wesness runners, with one credited run captain in each city. FRONT ROW culture-shapers. Westside store stylists and store staff, credited by name and store. In Pilot 01, about 15 to 30 Regulars from the launch store's catchment. Everyone filmed signs a release, and minors need guardian consent.
store_hook: RSVP to Regulars Night at your home store from Tuesday's post. Every perk is redeemed in a store: kit pickup, a place at the Thursday-night Window install before the members' 9 PM preview, trial-room shoot slots, priority Trial Room bookings and Regulars Night itself. Each Regular's home-store code is captured at the billing counter against their WestStyleClub ID. Runners check in at the store door with the route-card QR. Runs use only high-street stores with approved early access, or are timed to finish at opening, with chai and the activewear rail inside.
kpi: Footfall per store (entries) at each Regulars home store in brief weeks, against matched control stores. Regulars Night RSVPs per store, and the share who attend. Per Regular and home store: member-attributed bills and new WestStyleClub sign-ups, matched by WestStyleClub ID at the counter. Store-tagged posts per store; The Bench is scored on store-tagged posts and bills, not shares. Runners checked in at the store door, and their bills within seven days. The share of stores with three or more active Regulars.
art_direction: Regulars keep their own face, voice and language, inside three shot grammars and one monthly hero edit.
Natural light only: no ring lights and no face filters.
The location tag is always a named store, never just 'Westside'.
A fixed end card: white uppercase sans on black reading 'Seen at Westside, <store>, <city>', with the tier badge.
ASCI disclosure (#ad or #collab) sits in the first line of every caption template.
Humour lives here, not in brand production. The Indian shopping ritual is the joke, never the customer, the family or the product.
Hinglish as people speak it, always subtitled.
precedent: On 12 June 2026 Zara opened The Fold-er, a magazine section in its own app where creators write columns with a shop link under every photo. On 6 May 2026 Target replaced its creator programme with two, the gamified Club Target for everyday creators and the invite-only Target Ambassadors, powered by LTK, because creators 'don't all operate the same way'. Club Target rewards include features on Target's own social accounts, which The Regulars turns into a fixed Tuesday slot on @seenatwestside, with tiers scored at the store counter. Westside's Wesness runs already start at its stores, including Gachibowli (1 March 2026), New Commercial Street (12 April 2026) and Sky Vista DN Nagar II (26 April 2026). In 2026 the running community pushed back when Zara Athleticz named an ultrarunner its 'curator', so Wesness leaders are credited as run captains.
